correctness.rationale: Maximality forces exactly one representative of every cluster. With equal cluster size, the independent core-first indicators and iid cluster minima independent of them give the stated greedy law on the induced candidate set B. Intra-clique label permutations act transitively on each compatible private output, giving the same uniform conditional kernel under both laws and hence exact reduction of TV to core TV. Under the candidate law conditioned on independence, B has the uniform MIS core marginal ν, and greedy leaves B unchanged. Writing ε=Pr(B not independent) and ζ for the greedy core law conditional on this event gives μ=(1−ε)ν+εζ. Since ζ puts no mass on the empty set, εν(∅)≤TV(μ,ν)≤ε. Here ε=1−Z_H(t)/(1+t)^r=|E(H)|t²+O_H(t³) and ν(∅)=1+O_H(t). This proves the sharp coefficient and the exact empty-event obstruction. For a complete core, symmetry puts all opposite-signed discrepancies on the singletons, giving equality in the empty-event lower bound. For unequal positive sizes the candidate order need not be uniform, but the first candidate must still be accepted if B is nonempty; independence of the indicators gives the asserted all-private probability and the weighted all-subsets sum strictly dominates its independent part precisely when H has an edge.
residual_risks: The finite tests are ancillary. The expansion fixes H and does not apply uniformly as the core grows; no uniform candidate-order law is asserted for unequal sizes.
